items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: Nonetheless Letterman was really more spontaneous because yes you could do something over, we never did though in the first twelve years when we were on at 12:30 AM

ctx.x: Well it was really exciting on SNL, how live it was. At the beginning totally nerve wracking. I couldn’t believe it was going to happen during the rehearsals leading up to it. How complicated the production of the show was — I never had seen anything like it. The studio that seemed huge at the time, and they had so many different sets as they still do. You can see it on SNL now when the camera pulls back you see the studio with all

the different sets that they’re going to use during the half hour, all at different points, and how are they going to go from here to here? Well the whole camera’s like a big caravan drive down during the commercial to the other end. I said this is surreal but it certainly happened. And every time was pretty exciting because you know you don’t get a second chance, period. You don’t get a do-over. Nonetheless Letterman was really more spontaneous because yes you could do something over, we never did though in the…
I was going to ask if there was a “break glass in case of emergency” type protocol if you really had like a train wreck but it sounds like it just spontaneously fixed itself somehow.
